note: English Wikipedia places the ruins at 36° 01′ 04″ N, 9° 13′ 47″ E (the stored point), while the Digital Atlas of the Roman Empire gives 36.02994, 9.222872 with only 2000 m precision, 1.47 km away; no second independent source with printed coordinates could be found to confirm either point (Pleiades is behind a bot challenge), so the point is held for the owner.

Only C. Michael Hogan's Megalithic Portal entry gives a point for Careyeros Hill (20.783278N 105.522008W, matching the stored point); no gazetteer, register or second independent page gives the site's position, so a second source cannot be quoted.

Aliquot (Presses de l'Ifpo) and middleeast.com place the temple inside Bakka village, at the top of the village near the mosque, about 2.7 km NNE of the stored point (which falls in Kfar Qouq municipality), but no two independent pages print coordinates for the temple itself; the Wikipedia point is the village's, so the point is held for the owner.

The shield was dredged from the River Witham 'in the vicinity of Washingborough and Fiskerton'; the Lincolnshire HER findspot record MLI80991 states 'No mapped location recorded' and 'Grid reference Not recorded', so no source prints coordinates for the findspot.

Both the stored point (about 2.5 km off) and the Wikidata point (in Duas Igrejas village) are wrong: the shelter lies about 3 km out on the Douro escarpments near 41.4569, -6.3369 (Rota da Terra Fria map, OpenStreetMap, pt-wiki 41° 27′ 24″ N, 6° 20′ 12″ O). But only the Terras de Trás-os-Montes guide prints a point in a machine-readable form (pt-wiki uses 'O' for west), so two independent sources cannot be quoted.

The only published coordinates (Wikipedia/Wikidata, and an OpenStreetMap peak node tagged with the same Wikidata item) are those of the mountain T'akaq; no source gives the point of the archaeological site itself, which a local tourism page only places on the hill about 500 m from Chavinillo.

Only one source family prints a quotable point for the Theban Treasury: Wikidata Q22675693 (38°28'53.422"N, 22°30'4.540"E = 38.481506, 22.501261, 0.1 km from the stored point). OpenStreetMap maps the building (way 145690066, 'Θησαυρός Θηβαίων', centre 38.48150, 22.50121), but Mapcarta, the only page printing that point, prints each coordinate twice in two formats and cannot be quoted as one pair; ToposText, Pleiades, GeoNames and the Megalithic Portal have no entry for it.

The site is the Iron Age settlement and Roman villa north of the village near the River Welland, which RCHME and the Northamptonshire HER locate only by grid reference (centred SP 788917, about 52.517, -0.840, some 2 km north-west of the stored village point); no page gives its point in latitude and longitude, so it is held for the owner.

Ocean X never published the anomaly's position (esovitae.com: 'Ocean X Team has not published precise coordinates'), Wikipedia and Wikidata give none, and the web pages that print a point disagree by tens of kilometres (61.377 N 18.448 E on morbidkuriosity.com, 60.45 N 19.80 E on mysteria.co, 60.83 N 19.79 E on ancientworldatlas.com). No two independent sources agree on the point, so it is held for the owner.

The Wikidata point (28.094444, 35.200278) is the GeoNames point of the modern village of 'Aynunah, not the ruins. Pleiades (place 814698) puts the fortified settlement and the emporion at about 28.088-28.090, 35.184-35.186, within 0.4 km of the stored point, but its HTML page now sits behind an Anubis bot challenge. DARE gives only a 2 km-precision point. No two readable independent sources print the site's own coordinates, so the point is held for the owner.

The stored point lies in fields about 13.5 km east of the tell. Pleiades (OSM and CIGS locations), the German, Dutch and Polish Wikipedias (32°15′11″N 45°03′15″E) and satellite imagery put the main mound at about 32.2526, 45.0544, while English Wikipedia/Wikidata give a minute-rounded 32.2667, 45.0833, 3 km off. Only the Wikipedia family can be quoted: Pleiades now serves a bot challenge, CDLI prints the point longitude first and Mapcarta prints four values, so no second independent quotable source exists and the point is held for the owner (suggested 32.2526, 45.0544).

The entry names only the park; the stored point (about TQ 2054 7377) lies on no recorded barrow, and the park's recorded mounds - King Henry's Mound (TQ 1860 7315), the possible long barrow west of Queen's Road (TQ 1892 7212) and the destroyed Oliver's Mound (TQ 192 735) - lie 1.4 to 2.7 km away; the sources cannot settle which of them this entry is, so no two sources give this site's point and it is held for the owner.

Only the Wikipedia/Wikidata family prints a point for the site (9°22′14.65″S 77°7′47.50″W, 26 m from the stored point); the OSM-based Mapcarta page gives its point only as separate latitude/longitude lines and the provincial page and project blog give UTM grid references, so no second independent quotable point exists.

The site lies in dusun Tebing Tinggi, Kelurahan Lubuk Buntak, Kecamatan Dempo Selatan, Pagar Alam (Kumparan), and the stored point reverse-geocodes to Dempo Selatan, but no readable page prints coordinates for the site itself: the former BPCB Jambi page no longer resolves (its host is gone), and only the kelurahan's point is published. The point is held for the owner.

The Nazca lines cover some 450 km2 and the sources that print a point disagree by kilometres: Wikipedia gives 14°41′51″S 75°08′06″W (about 5 km from the stored point), the Megalithic Portal 14.695S 75.16W (2.7 km from Wikipedia's point), latlong.net -14.739025, -75.130135; no two independent sources agree within 1 km of one point or of the stored point, so the point is held for the owner.

Only Wikipedia (citing the UNESCO astronomical-heritage portal) gives a point for the arrangement, 37°52′30″S 144°27′28″E, which is the stored point; the Megalithic Portal gives 37.895149S 144.466250E but says these are the coordinates of the cultural centre nearby because the Aboriginal custodians have asked that the exact location not be made public, and the ICOMOS-IAU case study gives only whole degrees. No second independent source can be quoted for the site's point, so it is held for the owner (note the custodians' request).

Only the Wikipedia/Wikidata family prints a point for Kuntuyuq (-10.54944, -76.35917, 0.1 km from the stored point); MINCETUR's inventory shows none in its text and the tourism pages give only a UTM grid reference (18L 0350398 / 8834195), which is not read, so no two independent quotable sources exist.

Only English Wikipedia (7°38'56"S 77°25'05"W, which the stored point copies) gives a quotable point; OpenStreetMap (via Mapcarta, -7.65522, -77.40214) and the World Monuments Fund page (script data -7.656869, -77.406935) put the ruins 1.5-1.9 km further east-south-east, near the Wikipedia point's neighbour Los Pinchudos lying to the west, and neither prints its point in a quotable form, so no two independent sources agree on the site's point.

Neither Wikipedia nor Wikidata gives a point, and the MINCETUR inventory only places the ruins on Cerro Pucará near Antapite in the south of Concepción District; the stored point lies near the hamlet Alto Perú (Cariana, Vilcas Huamán), about 10 km from Antapite, and no source prints a quotable point for the ruins.

The rock shelter lies about an hour's walk from the village of Pacllon (MINCETUR inventory via turismoperuano), but no source prints its point. The Wikidata/Wikipedia point sits within 0.3 km of Pacllon village itself, and the stored point lies 8.5 km away in La Primavera district. With no two independent sources for the site's own point, it is held for the owner.

Wikipedia and Sabq place Jabal al-Baidain 13 km south-west of Dawadmi in Riyadh Region. The stored point (31.28, 36.29) lies in Jordan, about 1,100 km away, so it is wrong. Only GeoNames prints a point for the hill (Jabal al Baydatayn, GeonameId 107475: 24.47389, 44.24833), and no second independent source gives coordinates, so the point is held for the owner with that lead.
